newsitem.title: FRANCE: France, Netherlands to sign anti-drugs pact.
newsitem.headline: France, Netherlands to sign anti-drugs pact.

text.p: France, which has protested that the Dutch were too soft on drugs, said on Thursday it would sign an agreement with the Netherlands next week aimed at fighting drugs smuggling.

The agreement to step up cooperation between the two nations' customs authorities is a fresh sign of improving ties between Paris and the Hague, frayed by French accusations of Dutch leniency towards illegal drugs.

"France is delighted by the signing of this agreement as the Netherlands assumes the (rotating) presidency of the European Union," the French Budget Minister said in a statement announcing the signing.
The ministry is responsible for French customs.
"The agreement will contribute to a better harmonisation of our customs operations at EU entry points and will strengthen the protection provided its residents," the statement said.
The Netherlands has come under fire within the 15-member EU for its policy on drugs.

It has endorsed an EU campaign to crack down on the drugs smuggling problem but has resisted pressure to abandon policies allowing the use of small amounts of soft drugs and their sale in "coffee-shops".

France protests that Dutch laxity has led to thousands of young "tourists" flocking to the Netherlands to buy cheap and readily-available drugs which are then circulated in France and other neighbouring countries.

To show its unhappiness, Paris has maintained border controls at some key entry points, refusing to fully implement the Schengen agreement which aims to eliminate border controls between some European states, arguing that to do so would help terrorists and flood France with illegal drugs.

France said the new accord would reinforce customs cooperation between the two states, in combatting not only illegal drugs but also cross-border tax fraud and the smuggling of such other illicit goods as restricted agricultural and chemical products, radioactive materials, protected species and counterfeit goods.
The accord would also provide for the exchange of information and technology aimed at combatting smuggling, the ministry said.
